payload.because: The "leave it as history" reading mistakes what the event says. A phase_status_changed appended today does not claim the phase finished today; it records that today someone stated its status, which is exactly true, and the log keeps both the statement and its time. Rewriting the original events WOULD be a fiction, and that is the thing ruled out. The cost of leaving them is not cosmetic: status.ts scopes the digest's Current task and Next task lines to the active phase, so in every record whose active phase is a finished one those two lines — the most-read lines of the orientation block — are silently absent. That is 14 of the 16 records rendering degraded digests at every session start. A shipped `doctor --fix` is rejected on the standing rule that doctor never touches record prose (SPEC §CLI): the fix is a JUDGEMENT about whether work is finished, and a flag that makes that judgement for you is how a record stops meaning anything. payload.text:
A cross-record bookkeeping session MUST carry the target record's existing next action forward VERBATIM. sofar_end_session's next_action REPLACES whatever the record had — there is no merge and no append — so a session that writes into another initiative for a mechanical reason (a phase close, a status repair) and then writes back with its own next action has silently destroyed that record's real one. Nothing warns: the write-back succeeds, the digest renders, and the loss is only visible to someone who remembers what used to be there.

The discipline that makes it safe, used across all 16 records of the phase-lifecycle 4.3 repair: read `Next action:` off the target's plan.md BEFORE writing anything, and pass that string back unchanged. Put your own account of the visit in the `summary`, which has no such alias, and put any observation about the next action being stale in the summary too — never in the field itself. Editing another record's next action is a judgement belonging to that record's owner, even when you can see it is out of date.

Two traps ride along with it:
1. A token starting with `--` anywhere in end_session's args makes the write-back fail with a misleading "next_action: must be a non-empty string". cli-ui's next action contains `sofar status --watch`, so preserving it verbatim through the MCP tool is IMPOSSIBLE. The fallback that works and preserves bytes exactly: `sofar event append <slug> --type session_ended --session <id> --source claude-code --actor agent --payload '{"session_id":…,"summary":…,"next_action":…}'` — one JSON string sidesteps the multi-arg handling. Note the explicit <slug>, which is what keeps that CLI write off the branch resolver (record-integrity M1).
2. session_ended is LAST-WINS, so a write-back with a mangled next action is repairable: append another one with the correct text and the projection re-renders. Verified live this session after paraphrasing commit-attribution's publish command instead of preserving it.

sofar_update_plan ERASES phase and task status unless the caller restates it. plan_updated is a FULL REPLACE: mcp/update-plan.ts appends the caller's payload verbatim with no carry-forward, and the fold rebuilds state.phases from it taking `phase.status ?? 'pending'` and `task.status ?? 'pending'` (core/fold.ts:1085-1091). So an update_plan that omits statuses silently resets every phase to pending and every task to pending, and nothing warns — the fold is doing exactly what it was told.

This is the documented contract for tasks (task-drop-state D2, on which SPEC's forward-compatibility story rests) and every real payload in this repo's record does carry statuses through. It is newly LOAD-BEARING for phases: before 0.27.0 phase status was barely written, and now 34 retroactive closes across 16 still-active records sit on top of it (phase-lifecycle 4.3). One careless replan in any of those records re-inflates the stale-phase count with no signal that anything was lost.

HOW TO APPLY: before calling sofar_update_plan, fold the current state and copy each phase's and task's existing status into the payload — never hand-build a plan from prose. If a replan is genuinely meant to reset progress, say so in the session write-back, because the log cannot distinguish that intent from an omission.

DIAGNOSE BY: a record whose phases all read pending immediately after a plan edit, or a stale-phase count that climbs with no phase work having happened. Found by phase-lifecycle's final review 2026-08-13, unfixed and deliberately so — the fix would be a carry-forward merge in update-plan.ts, which needs a Decision first because it changes the full-replace contract.

payload.text: BUG filed from self-improve (sofar-37, 2026-09-23, at sofar-c3's direction; phase-lifecycle owns sofar_update_phase and phase notes are its surface). sofar_update_plan silently DROPS every phase note. The note has no field in the update_plan schema, so a caller who restates every phase and task correctly still loses the summaries rendered under each phase heading in plan.md. MEASURED twice tonight while adding tasks 3.5 and 3.6 to self-improve: both replaces preserved all 4 phases and all task statuses, and both silently removed the Phase 1 and Phase 2 notes; re-issuing sofar_update_phase with the same status and the note verbatim restores them, and a diff of plan.md against a copy taken before the call is what caught it. WHY THIS IS A FIX AND NOT MORE DOCUMENTATION: the workaround is ALREADY in repo memory (.sofar/repo.md, "after ANY sofar_update_plan, re-issue sofar_update_phase for every phase that had a note, because plan_updated drops notes silently") and an experienced session walked into it anyway. A documented workaround that is still walked into is evidence that documentation is not the fix. SHAPE: this is the same family as round-1 loss row L11, which self-improve's cycle-L11b studied tonight — a full-replace write path that silently discards data the caller could not express, there a plan update wiping phases 6–8, here a plan update wiping phase notes. Candidate fixes, for whoever picks it up: carry notes through the replace by preserving the note of any phase whose name is unchanged; or accept an optional note per phase in the update_plan schema; or refuse a replace that would drop a note unless it is restated. The operator is being asked tonight whether L11 gets a new fix attempt, and sofar-c3 asked for these two to go in front of them together, as one family.

payload.because: Both bugs discard caller intent without saying so, and both were found by the same night's work: L11 by the evaluator's replay of round 1's recorded calls, the note-dropping by a session adding a task to its own plan. A caller who is told nothing cannot correct anything, which is why the rule is about reporting and preserving rather than about either specific field.
payload.chose: OPERATOR RULING 2026-09-23, relayed by sofar-c3 and filed here by self-improve (sofar-37) because this initiative owns sofar_update_phase and phase notes. TWO BUGS, ONE FAMILY, ONE CHANGE: a plan-or-phase write path that silently refuses or discards data because the shape it was handed has no slot in the schema. (1) sofar_update_phase refuses a BARE phase name where the plan names the phase "7. Suggestions & transport" — round-1 loss row L11, 2 invalid_input in claude-sofar/r3 S7 and S8, and the refusal is what led to the S9 full-replace plan update that wiped phases 6–8. The fix is exact and needs no further experiment: accept a phase name that matches after a leading ordinal is stripped ("7. ", "7 ", "7)"), alongside the number and the case-insensitive full name already accepted. (2) sofar_update_plan silently drops every phase NOTE, because the note has no field in its schema: phases, tasks and statuses survive a full replace and the summaries do not. Measured twice on 2026-09-22 in self-improve, the second time by a session that had just written the warning itself (self-improve M8). THE EVALUATOR IS NOT RE-RUN FOR THIS: cycle-L11b's DISCARD is a verdict on the LOOP — whether its brief beat an equal-budget baseline — and not on whether L11 should be fixed. Conflating them would leave a real bug unfixed because a meta-experiment came back negative, and another cycle would spend about $18 and 2.5 h rediscovering a diagnosis this one already produced. The evaluator earns its cost on fixes that cannot be reasoned to; this one can.
